text: Place value means the value of a digit depends on its position in a number. For example, in the number 4,582, the digit 4 means four thousands, the digit 5 means five hundreds, the digit 8 means eight tens, and the digit 2 means two ones.
Worked example: What is the value of 7 in 37,421? The digit 7 is in the thousands place, so its value is 7,000.
Practice questions: 1. What is the value of 6 in 46,210? 2. What is the value of 3 in 305,981? 3. Write 52,709 in expanded form.
Common mistake: Students sometimes confuse the digit with its value. In 68,000, the digit is 6, but its value is 60,000 because it is in the ten-thousands place.

Rounding means changing a number to a nearby value that is easier to use. When rounding to the nearest ten, hundred, or thousand, look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to. If that digit is 5 or more, round up. If it is 4 or less, keep the digit the same.
Worked example: Round 34,682 to the nearest thousand. Look at the hundreds digit, which is 6. Since 6 is 5 or more, round the thousands digit up. 34,682 rounded to the nearest thousand is 35,000.
Practice questions: 1. Round 27,346 to the nearest thousand. 2. Round 8,751 to the nearest hundred. 3. Round 63,219 to the nearest ten.

Common mistake: Students sometimes look at the wrong digit when rounding. For example, when rounding 34,682 to the nearest thousand, they should look at the hundreds digit, not the tens or ones digit.
